text:
mike: quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a seam matrix for hosted -> dedicated -> private migrations. trying to capture: config translation, auth mapping, network quarantine, rollback isolation. thoughts?

elena: love a matrix. can you paste the minimal example so we can iterate?

mike: pasted below. it's intentionally compact.

```
Seam | Hosted config | Dedicated mapping | Private notes
---|---|---|---
model_variant | model_id -> pinned_model_id | same, but customer override allowed | config encrypt + local path support
auth | api-key + tenant | mTLS + tenant-id header | KMS-integrated tokens
routing | region auto | region pin per-tenant | network ACLs + no public egress
metrics | host-level | dedicated exporter | local stats relay -> central
```

sameer: couple of immediate red flags: 1) assumptions about token formats when mapping hosted api-key -> mTLS. 2) KV cache expectations (shared vs isolated).

tara: agree. also need a quarantine mode for model variants that fail safety checks in private envs — we shouldn't auto-fallback to hosted in that case.

ryan: why not? fallback keeps availability.

tara: because private customers may require strict data residency + no outbound to hosted. fallback could violate compliance. we need a policy layer: `allow_fallback: true|false` per-tenant.

elena: +1 for per-tenant policy. add a global default in control plane that Dedicated honors unless customer overrides. That reduces surprises.

mike: proposed control-plane contract snippet (pseudocode):

```
route_policy {
  allow_fallback: boolean
  preferred_tier: [HOSTED, DEDICATED, PRIVATE]
  compat_versions: ["v1.2", "v1.3"]
}
```

ryan: compat_versions seems important. we should also include `min_runtime_features` so adapters can short-circuit early.

sameer: about KV cache — runtime adapters must expose `cache_namespace` and `isolation_level`. if migrating tenant, we can remap namespace but must rehydrate prefix cache gradually.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: RFC "seam-matrix-v1" published: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/834

sophia: testing strategy idea: use a staged traffic runner. start 2% traffic through the adapter shim, validate latency and correctness against golden outputs, then ramp. capture per-route diffs.

mike: agree. also need a migration tool that can do "dry-run remap" to show predicted conflicts (auth format mismatches, param names).

elena: audit logs: when we translate hosted config -> dedicated/private, record the translation delta as an entry. useful for debugging and compliance.

ryan: on the SDK surface, we should avoid changing client behavior. translate on the control plane so SDKs remain stable. only expose migration status via admin APIs.

sameer: one more: health signaling. Adapters should publish a `quarantine` health state separate from `unhealthy` so control plane can decide to route around without marking cluster unhealthy.

mike: nice. summary actions: 1) add allow_fallback policy 2) define adapter interface fields (cache_namespace, isolation_level, min_runtime_features, quarantine_state) 3) audit translations + dry-run tool 4) staged runner + diffs.

tara: i'll take 2 and work with eng-runtime to draft an adapter proto.

elena: i'll own 3 (translation audit + CLI dry-run).

sophia: i'll prototype the staged runner harness.

mike: great. tagging this thread into the RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:
